# @ic-reactor/core — AI Quick Guide

Framework-agnostic runtime for IC apps. Use this when you are not writing
React hooks directly.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/core @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/query-core
```

## Core Building Blocks

- `ClientManager` for shared agent + QueryClient state
- `Reactor` for raw Candid values
- `DisplayReactor` for UI-friendly transformed values

## Preferred Usage

- Reuse one `ClientManager` across multiple canisters
- Use `fetchQuery` / `getQueryData` / `invalidateQueries` for cache-aware calls
- `invalidateQueries` returns TanStack Query's `Promise<void>`: `await` it to
  wait until the active queries it matched have refetched (a failed refetch
  does not reject it); prefix a call you do not wait for with `void`
- A sign-in or sign-out cancels a `fetchQuery` in flight; it then fetches again
  for the new identity and resolves with that answer, never with TanStack's
  `CancelledError`. Wrap other imperative fetches of canister queries (for
  example `queryClient.fetchQuery` or `queryClient.fetchInfiniteQuery`) in
  `clientManager.fetchAcrossIdentitySwitch(() => ...)` for the same behaviour:
  unwrapped, a cancelled refetch of a stale entry resolves with the previous
  principal's cached data. After 3 runs each overtaken by another switch it
  rejects with a `CallError`
- Use `callMethod` for imperative update/query calls
- Several canisters of one interface (a multi-token wallet): build one reactor
  and call `reactor.forCanister(canisterId)` for each other canister. It gives a
  memoized sibling of the same class on the same `ClientManager`, with the
  interface, polling options and validators, keyed by its own canister. Do not
  retarget a shared reactor with `setCanisterId` or hand-build one reactor per
  canister

## DisplayReactor Guidance

- Choose `DisplayReactor` when users type/read principals and numbers in forms
- Validation can run on display values before calls
- Pass the service type (`new DisplayReactor<_SERVICE>(...)`). Without it the
  display-side args, validator args and results are `unknown` (an untyped
  `Reactor` gives `any`); cast to the display shape only when the interface is
  known only at run time
- `fromZodSchema(schema, { async: true })` for a zod schema with async
  refinements; async validators run only in `validate()` and
  `callMethodWithValidation()` (`callMethod()` and the React hooks refuse them)
- Floats display as numbers and `NaN`/`±Infinity`/`-0` are sent back as read,
  but JSON writes `NaN`/`±Infinity` as `null` and `-0` as `0`: after a JSON
  round trip an `opt` float that held `NaN` is sent as none
- `vec record { text; T }` displays as an object: a repeated key keeps its last
  value and integer-like keys come first in ascending order. Use `Reactor`
  where repeated keys or their order matter (HTTP headers, ICRC-21 fields)

## Token Amounts

- Ledger amounts are base units (e8s): a `bigint` from `Reactor`, integer text
  from `DisplayReactor`. Never convert them with `Number`, `parseFloat`,
  `Math.pow` or `toFixed`: `Math.floor(Number("0.29") * 10 ** 8)` is 28999999
- Show one with `formatTokenAmount(value, decimals, { maxFractionDigits?,
  minFractionDigits?, trimTrailingZeros?, roundingMode?, locale?, useGrouping? })`;
  it takes the reactor's value and `icrc1_decimals` as returned, truncates past
  `maxFractionDigits` unless `roundingMode: "halfExpand"`, and is plain text
  (`"1234.5"`) unless given a `locale`
- Read typed text with `parseTokenAmount(text, decimals)`, which returns a
  `bigint` and throws a `TypeError` for text that is not digits with one `.`
  (grouping, exponents) and a `RangeError` for more fraction digits than the
  token has or a negative amount (`{ allowNegative: true }` for an `int`).
  Pass `amount.toString()` to a `DisplayReactor`

```ts
const amount = parseTokenAmount(input, decimals) // "0.29", 8 -> 29000000n
await ledger.callMethod({
  functionName: "icrc1_transfer",
  args: [{ to: { owner }, amount: amount.toString() }], // DisplayReactor
})
formatTokenAmount(balance, decimals, { maxFractionDigits: 4 }) // "1.2345"
```

## Principal Text

- Validate a principal a person typed with `isPrincipalText(text.trim())`
  rather than `try { Principal.fromText(text) } catch {}`. It accepts only
  canonical text of at most 29 bytes (not the `{"__principal__":…}` JSON form
  `Principal.fromText` also reads) and never throws. A `DisplayReactor`
  takes the text; a `Reactor` takes `Principal.fromText(text)`

## Showing Raw Values

- `jsonToString(value)` is `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` that writes a
  `bigint` as its digits, a `Principal` as its text and a `Uint8Array` as hex.
  Use it to print a result instead of writing a BigInt replacer by hand

## Local Environment Root Key

In a browser with no `agentOptions.host`, the agent routes through the page
origin when the page is local (`localhost`, loopback), a Codespaces or Gitpod
domain (`network: "remote"`), or an IC boundary domain; any other page falls
back to mainnet.

The `ic_env` cookie is trusted only for hosts that `allowsEnvRootKey(host)`
accepts: loopback (all of 127.0.0.0/8 and `::1`), and `localhost` and its
subdomains. Cookies are not origin-isolated, so this is a positive allowlist —
any other host (custom domain, tunnel, staging, and Codespaces or Gitpod, whose
workspaces share a parent domain with strangers') must opt in with
`allowEnvConfig: true` on
`ClientManagerParameters`. The deprecated `allowEnvRootKey` still works but is
scoped to what it always granted — the root key alone — so it does not make
`trustsEnvConfig` true.

That one decision is resolved once in the constructor and exposed as
`clientManager.trustsEnvConfig`. It governs all three values the cookie carries:
the root key (without it, a local agent fetches the key from the replica before
its first request, unless `shouldFetchRootKey` is `false`), the Internet
Identity provider, and the `PUBLIC_CANISTER_ID:<name>` entry
a `Reactor` resolves when no `canisterId` is configured. On an untrusted host a
reactor with no configured id throws rather than reading the cookie — a
substituted canister id still verifies against the real mainnet root key, so
certificate verification cannot catch it.

On a host whose network isn't `"ic"`, `ClientManager.initialize()` fetches the
replica's root key and replaces the cookie's key, or mainnet's under
`shouldFetchRootKey: false` with no key. A key passed as `agentOptions.rootKey`
is kept: `initialize()` fetches nothing, resolves even when the replica's status
endpoint is unreachable, and every call is verified against that key
(`clientManager.explicitRootKey` reports it). On a mainnet host nothing is
fetched.

`isMainnetHost` is a boundary-node check only; it recognises three canonical
domains and returns `false` for a mainnet dapp on a custom domain. Never use it
as a "safe to trust local configuration" test.

## Types From a Reactor

Read a method's types off the reactor instead of spelling out the service and
transform: `ReactorArgsOf<typeof ledger, "icrc1_balance_of">[0]` (the account
in the reactor's form), `ReactorDataOf<typeof ledger, M>` (what the call
resolves with), `ReactorErrorOf<typeof ledger, M>` (a hook's `error`), plus
`ServiceOf<typeof ledger>` and `TransformOf<typeof ledger>`. They replace
`ReactorArgs<_SERVICE, M, "display">` and friends and hand-written copies of
display types. They work for `Reactor`, `DisplayReactor` and any subclass.

## Error Types

- `CanisterError`: canister `Result.Err`
- `CallError`: transport/agent failures, and a validator that threw
  (the thrown value is `cause`)
- `ValidationError`: display-validator failures

## Retries

- `reactorRetry` / `isRetryableReactorError`: retry only what could change —
  transport, certificate, HTTP 5xx/408/429, `SysTransient`/`SysUnknown`. Never
  a `CanisterError`, a `ValidationError`, an encode/decode failure or another
  HTTP 4xx (an expired delegation's 400, a 403).
- An update call runs again on every attempt. `reactorUpdateRetry` /
  `isRetryableUpdateError` retry only a `SysTransient` rejection, which proves
  the call never ran. `getQueryOptions` and `fetchQuery` give an update method
  a retry of only `SysTransient`, as often as the QueryClient's `retry`
  default allows (`Reactor.getQueryRetry`), unless the caller sets `retry`.

## Generated Files

If generated declarations are wrong, change source `.did` or codegen templates.
Do not hand-edit generated output.
